objectives: Blend /k/ with short vowels and final consonants.
Discriminate short-vowel changes in /k/ CVC words.
Repair decoding errors by checking the middle vowel.
concepts: Blending joins phonemes into a spoken word.
The middle vowel can change the word even when the first and last sounds stay constant.
Accurate decoding should be confirmed by rereading the whole word.

definitions.definition: Combining individual phonemes smoothly to read a word.
Checking the middle vowel sound when two CVC words are confused.

workedExamples: If cup is read as cap, return to the middle vowel and blend again.
commonMistakes: Saying letter names instead of phonemes.

basic: Blend /k/ CVC words with short vowels.
conceptual: Identify how the middle vowel changes a decoded word.
application: Repair CVC decoding errors using phoneme-by-phoneme analysis.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why guessing from the first letter is unreliable.
mixedReview: Decode /k/ CVC words across multiple short vowels.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC decoding = first sound + middle vowel + final sound
mistakeBasedRevision: If two words are confused, isolate and compare the middle vowel.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat short-vowel /k/ CVC contrasts using fresh words.

activities.name: Repair and reread
steps: Identify the incorrect vowel if present.

outcomes: Learner uses rereading to confirm accurate decoding.
